source.en: 本文件是英文文案的单一真相；src/shared/nodes/i18n/catalog.en-US.ts 由 scripts/i18n-build-catalog.mjs 生成

message_received.label: Message received
message_received.description: Message trigger (match modes: any message / @bot / command / keyword / regex)
message_received.summary: Fires when a chat message arrives. Match modes: any message / @bot / command / keyword / regex (capture-group extraction supported)

outputs.args.name: Command args
outputs.args.description: Command arguments (only in "command" mode; empty list in other modes)

outputs.ark_type.name: Card type
outputs.ark_type.description: The official ark message type (for example picture); empty for plain text messages. The picture value was added by the official API on 2026-09-16

outputs.matched.name: Matched text
outputs.matched.description: The full regex match (only in "regex" mode; empty string in other modes)

outputs.groups.name: Capture group
outputs.groups.description: List of regex capture groups (only in "regex" mode; empty list in other modes)

scheduled.label: Scheduled trigger
scheduled.summary: Trigger on a Cron expression or a fixed interval — for scheduled pushes and polling tasks

request_received.label: Request event
request_received.description: Listen for group join requests / invites (the only "request" event the official API has; **adding a friend is NOT a request event** — it arrives as "Notice event → user added the bot")
request_received.summary: Fires when a user applies to join the group, or a member invites the bot into a group — commonly used to auto-approve joins. There is NO such thing as a "friend request": friend-adding is a notice event, not an approvable request, so do not wait for it here

outputs.request_type.name: Request type
outputs.request_type.description: The type actually received: under the official API there is only "group join request / invite" (value group)

outputs.user_id.name: User QQ
outputs.user_id.description: QQ number that sent the request

outputs.group_id.name: Group
outputs.group_id.description: Group number being joined (group messages only)

outputs.flag.name: Flag
outputs.flag.description: Request flag, passed back when approving or rejecting

notice_received.label: Notice event
notice_received.description: Listen for notice events: member joined / left, message audit result, interaction
notice_received.summary: Listen for notice events (optionally filtered by type) — for welcome messages, leave alerts and audit-result handling. The receivable types are exactly the ones in the "Notice type" dropdown (whatever the official adapter emits is what is listed there)

outputs.notice_type.name: Notice type
outputs.notice_type.description: Actually received type (the official adapter emits group_member_add / group_member_remove / message_audit / interaction etc. — see the values in the "Notice type" dropdown)

outputs.user_id.name: Target QQ
outputs.user_id.description: QQ number of the affected user

outputs.group_id.name: Group
outputs.group_id.description: Group number where the event happened

outputs.sub_type.name: Sub type
outputs.sub_type.description: Notice sub type: approve / invite / leave / kick, etc.

outputs.operator_id.name: Operator QQ
outputs.operator_id.description: User who performed the action (inviter or admin for join/leave events; 0 when absent)

button_clicked.label: Button click
button_clicked.description: Listen for button / quick-menu clicks (QQ official INTERACTION_CREATE event)
button_clicked.summary: Fires when a user clicks a button in a button UI or a quick menu. The official API pushes INTERACTION_CREATE (intent 1<<26) and the framework subscribes automatically (falls back and logs when unauthorized). Wire "Interaction ID" into the "Button response" node to acknowledge; the client keeps spinning until timeout if you do not reply within 3 seconds

outputs.button_id.name: Button ID
outputs.button_id.description: ID of the clicked button (QQ official API)

outputs.button_data.name: Button data
outputs.button_data.description: The button's action_data (the data field set when configuring the button)

outputs.user_id.name: Clicker QQ
outputs.user_id.description: QQ number of the user who clicked

outputs.group_id.name: Group
outputs.group_id.description: Group number the button belongs to (empty in private chat)

outputs.interaction_id.name: Interaction ID
outputs.interaction_id.description: Interaction ID of this click; pass it to the "Button response" node to acknowledge (valid for 3 seconds)

on_ready.label: Connection ready
on_ready.description: Fires automatically once the bot connection is ready (lifecycle trigger)
on_ready.summary: Fires automatically once the bot connects — for startup notices, data initialization, cache warm-up and registering scheduled tasks. Multiple "Connection ready" triggers run in order. Each runtime instance fires it only once (not on reconnect; never before connecting)

outputs.event.name: Event object
outputs.event.description: Synthetic event object (no real user message; for downstream nodes to reference)

outputs.ready_at.name: Ready at
outputs.ready_at.description: Unix timestamp when the bot connection became ready (seconds)

on_startup.label: Bot startup
on_startup.description: Fires automatically when the TS runtime starts (lifecycle trigger, earlier than connection ready)
on_startup.summary: Fires when the runtime (FlowRuntime) starts, earlier than "Connection ready" (the translator gateway is not connected yet). Only suitable for initialization that sends no messages: creating database tables, loading config, warming caches. Use "Connection ready" if you need to send messages

outputs.event.name: Event object
outputs.event.description: Synthetic event object (no real user message; for downstream nodes to reference)

outputs.started_at.name: Started at
outputs.started_at.description: Unix timestamp when the driver started (seconds)

message_send.label: Send message
message_send.description: Send a message (plain text / Button UI / message segment / forward — four modes)
message_send.summary: Send a message (plain text / Button UI / message segment / forward × reply / proactive push). Choose the format as needed; the destination is decided by "Target type / Target ID".

inputs.mode.name: Mode
inputs.mode.description: Options: plain text / Button UI / message segment / forward

inputs.text.name: Text content
inputs.text.description: The text to send (used in plain-text mode; when empty, the upstream output bound via the data source is used). Supports the {var1}~{var4} placeholders: wire an upstream value into the matching "Variable N" port to interpolate it directly — no extra "Text template" node needed. Use "Text template" only when you need more than 4 placeholders or want to reuse the same text.

inputs.markdown.name: Markdown text
inputs.markdown.description: The message's Markdown content (Button UI mode; buttons must accompany a Markdown message). Also supports the {var1}~{var4} placeholders

inputs.force_verify_image_resource.name: Fail when the image cannot be mirrored
inputs.force_verify_image_resource.description: Added by the official API on 2026-08-10 (Markdown messages only): abort the send and return a failure when the image cannot be mirrored. Off by default, which keeps the old behaviour of sending anyway (the card will be missing its image)

inputs.keyboard.name: Button config
inputs.keyboard.description: InlineKeyboard config (Button UI mode, rows/buttons structure)

inputs.segments.name: Message segment
inputs.segments.description: Message segment: a dict or a list of dicts (message segment mode)

inputs.messages.name: Message list
inputs.messages.description: Forward message list as JSON ("forward" mode, [{"content":"...","user_id":"123","name":"nickname"}])

inputs.user_id.name: QQ number
inputs.user_id.description: Sender QQ for "forward" mode (empty = current user)

inputs.media_url.name: Media URL
inputs.media_url.description: Media to send (required in rich-media mode). Two accepted forms: an http(s) direct link, which the official QQ API fetches server-side (must be publicly reachable); or an absolute path to a local file, which goes through the official chunked upload and needs no public exposure (image/video/voice/file up to 200MB)

inputs.file_name.name: File name
inputs.file_name.description: File name shown when sending as a file (optional)

inputs.reply_to.name: Reply to
inputs.reply_to.description: The message to quote: use the message id in the current session, or wire in the value of "Get context → Reference ID". The official REFIDX is resolved by the adapter and reports a clear error when unavailable. "Forward" mode does not support quoting

inputs.is_wakeup.name: Interaction recall
inputs.is_wakeup.description: Interaction recall message (official is_wakeup, **private-chat push only**). The official API allocates a quota per 4 periods within 30 days; exceeding it is rejected server-side — the quota is decided by the official API, so it is not blocked locally and the error is passed through as-is. It is mutually exclusive with event_id / msg_id: when enabled those two fields are no longer sent

inputs.stream_content_type.name: Stream content format
inputs.stream_content_type.description: Text / Markdown (the official stream API's content_type, stream-message mode only)

inputs.stream_chunk_size.name: Chunk size
inputs.stream_chunk_size.description: Length of each chunk in characters (default 50). The node splits "Text content" into chunks and sends them one by one, marking the last chunk as finished; 0 or a negative number falls back to the default

inputs.stream_interval_ms.name: Chunk interval (ms)
inputs.stream_interval_ms.description: Wait between two consecutive chunks (default 300 ms). The official rate limit is 50 QPS, so do not set this too low

inputs.input_second.name: Duration (seconds)
inputs.input_second.description: How many seconds the "typing" indicator stays on (official cap is 60; larger values are clamped; leave empty for 30). The other side sees a typing indicator for that long.

inputs.ark_template_id.name: Card template ID
inputs.ark_template_id.description: Template id of an official structured card (documented values: 23 link + text list / 24 text + thumbnail / 37 large image). A card is "pick a template, fill its variables", and the template decides which variables exist. Requires admission approval from QQ platform operations.

inputs.ark_kv.name: Card variables
inputs.ark_kv.description: JSON array of template variables, e.g. [{"key":"#DESC#","value":"notice"}]. Array-typed variables nest through obj/obj_kv: [{"key":"#LIST#","obj":[{"obj_kv":[{"key":"desc","value":"reviewed"}]}]}]. Keys must match the chosen template exactly (such as #DESC# / #PROMPT# / #TITLE#).

inputs.embed_title.name: Card title
inputs.embed_title.description: Title of the Embed card. `title` is the only required field in an official Embed.

inputs.embed_prompt.name: Card prompt
inputs.embed_prompt.description: Small caption in the corner of the card (the official example uses it for the source, such as "notification").

inputs.embed_thumbnail.name: Thumbnail URL
inputs.embed_thumbnail.description: http(s) direct link to the thumbnail on the right (optional; leave empty to omit).

inputs.embed_fields.name: Card fields
inputs.embed_fields.description: Lines of body text in the card, as a JSON array: ["Current rank: Gold","Previous rank: Silver"], or [{"name":"Current rank: Gold"}]. Each entry is one line.

inputs.target_type.name: Target type
inputs.target_type.description: Empty means reply in the current session; you can also push to a private chat or a group

inputs.target_id.name: Target ID
inputs.target_id.description: Target ID (required when target_type is set)

outputs.message_id.name: Message ID
outputs.message_id.description: ID of the sent message (may be empty in plain-text mode)

message_recall.label: Recall
message_recall.summary: Recall a message by ID — handy for taking back a mis-sent message quickly

inputs.message_id.name: Message ID
inputs.message_id.description: ID of the message to recall (as a string)

message_edit.label: Edit message
message_edit.description: Edit an already-sent message (requires adapter support)
message_edit.summary: Edit a sent message by ID. Note: this depends on the adapter supporting the "edit message" API; when unsupported the call returns an error without breaking the flow

inputs.message_id.name: Message ID
inputs.message_id.description: ID of the message to edit

message_op.label: Build message segment
message_op.description: Build a message segment without sending it; segment_type switches between 9 segment types
message_op.summary: Build one message segment (@mention, image, face, voice, share, music, poke, reply, forward) and hand it to "Send message" to send as a segment

inputs.segment_type.name: Segment type
inputs.segment_type.description: Options: @mention / image / QQ face / voice / link share / music share / poke / reply / forward

inputs.user_id.name: QQ number
inputs.user_id.description: Message segment for "@mention / poke": QQ number

inputs.url.name: URL
inputs.url.description: Message segment for "image / voice / link share / music share": resource URL

inputs.file.name: File
inputs.file.description: Message segment for "image / voice": local file path

inputs.title.name: Title
inputs.title.description: Message segment for "link share / music share": title

inputs.content.name: Content
inputs.content.description: Message segment for "link share": share content

inputs.image_url.name: Image URL
inputs.image_url.description: Message segment for "link share / music share": cover image URL

inputs.music_type.name: Music type
inputs.music_type.description: Source of the message segment: NetEase Cloud Music / QQ Music / custom

inputs.audio_url.name: Audio URL
inputs.audio_url.description: "Music share · custom" message segment: direct audio URL

inputs.singer.name: Artist
inputs.singer.description: "Music share · custom" message segment: artist name

inputs.message_id.name: Message ID
inputs.message_id.description: "Reply" message segment: ID of the message to reply to

message_compose.label: Compose message
message_compose.description: Compose title/stats/quote/buttons/tappable commands into a card or list without sending it; hand it to "Send message" (Button UI mode)
message_compose.summary: Compose a markdown card or list, optionally with buttons or tappable command tags. Line breaks, alignment and the mandatory button fields are handled here — no string concatenation. Wire the result into "Send message" with mode = Button UI.

inputs.layout.name: Layout
inputs.layout.description: Options: card (title + stats + quote) / list (items + empty-state hint)

inputs.title.name: Title
inputs.title.description: Large bold title (markdown "#"), e.g. "Echo of the World"

inputs.subtitle.name: Subtitle
inputs.subtitle.description: One bold line under the title, e.g. "[Who] did what"

inputs.body.name: Body
inputs.body.description: Body lines: an array (one item per line) or multi-line text

inputs.stats.name: Stats
inputs.stats.description: Name→value table, auto-aligned. Accepts an object {"Level":"Lv3"}, pairs [["Level","Lv3"]] or "Level:Lv3" multi-line text

inputs.quote.name: Quote
inputs.quote.description: Grey-bar quote block (markdown ">") for a narration or hint. Multi-line input gets ">" on every line

inputs.footer.name: Footer
inputs.footer.description: One bottom line (e.g. "Obtained: Treasure Box ×1"), separated by a blank line

inputs.buttons.name: Button
inputs.buttons.description: Button rows: an array of rows, each row an array of buttons. A button is "text" (text = command) or {label,data} / {label,url}. Limit 5 rows × 5 buttons; overflow is trimmed and reported

inputs.buttons_json.name: Buttons (JSON)
inputs.buttons_json.description: JSON-string form of the buttons (for upstream nodes that already built JSON). Use instead of "Buttons"; "Buttons" wins when both are set

inputs.inline_commands.name: Tappable commands
inputs.inline_commands.description: A piece of **tappable text inside the body** (official names: command-input / command-enter). Same shape as "Buttons": outer array = rows, inner = tags in that row. Write `"/checkin"` directly; to show `[checkin]` but send `/checkin`, write `{label:"[checkin]",data:"/checkin"}`. A tap **fills the input box** by default (works everywhere); the tappable-command editor can switch it to sending straight away, which is officially **unsupported in group chats**

inputs.items.name: List items
inputs.items.description: For the list layout: an array (one item per line) or multi-line text

inputs.empty_text.name: Empty text
inputs.empty_text.description: For the list layout: shown when there is no data (a fallback is used when empty)

inputs.page.name: Page
inputs.page.description: List layout only: paging turns on when this is set (1-based). When one page does not fit, items and buttons are sliced and a "Previous / Next" row is appended

inputs.page_size.name: Items per page
inputs.page_size.description: Items per page when paging (default 8). Lowered automatically to fit the 5-row button budget, with a warning

inputs.page_command.name: Paging command
inputs.page_command.description: Command prefix the paging buttons send (e.g. `/shop all`); the page number is appended. Leave empty to send only the number

inputs.paging_json.name: Paging (JSON)
inputs.paging_json.description: Full paging config (object or JSON string) for advanced fields: fixedRows (a button row present on every page, e.g. "back") and footerHint. Overrides the simple fields above

inputs.max_length.name: Length limit
inputs.max_length.description: Markdown character limit; exceeding it raises an error (truncation would break the syntax, so it is not done automatically)

outputs.markdown.name: Markdown
outputs.markdown.description: Composed markdown → wire into the "markdown" port of "Send message" (Button UI mode)

outputs.keyboard.name: Button config
outputs.keyboard.description: Composed InlineKeyboard → wire into the "keyboard" port of "Send message"

outputs.button_count.name: Button rows
outputs.button_count.description: How many button rows (0 = no buttons, a plain markdown card)

outputs.success.name: Success
outputs.success.description: Whether a sendable message was composed

outputs.error.name: Error
outputs.error.description: Error message (empty = success). Button overflow, missing markdown and over-length are reported here

outputs.warnings.name: Warnings
outputs.warnings.description: Non-fatal warnings (trimmed buttons, buttons that do nothing when clicked); surfaced instead of being dropped silently

battle_panel.label: Battle panel
battle_panel.description: Turn-based battle panel (compose only, does not send): monster info + player info + round log + action buttons; outputs markdown and a keyboard
battle_panel.summary: Compose the battle state into one button message (monster/player HP, round log, attack / skill / item / flee). Re-sending it each round is how the panel "refreshes", because the official API cannot edit a sent message.

inputs.monster_level.name: Monster level
inputs.monster_level.description: Shown as "Slime Lv.1" when filled; empty shows the name only

inputs.monster_tag.name: Monster tag
inputs.monster_tag.description: The small line under the name, e.g. "normal" / "elite" / "BOSS"

inputs.monster_max_hp.name: Monster max HP
inputs.monster_max_hp.description: Upper bound (0 means no bar is drawn, avoiding a fake 0/0)

inputs.player_name.name: Player name
inputs.player_name.description: How the player is called inside the panel

inputs.player_mp.name: Player MP
inputs.player_mp.description: Current MP (leave empty and the "MP" line does not appear at all)

inputs.log.name: Round log
inputs.log.description: What happened this round (multi-line text, one entry per line)

inputs.footer.name: Footer
inputs.footer.description: Bottom quote block: drops, experience, hints

inputs.actions.name: Action buttons
inputs.actions.description: Button labels, comma or space separated (up to 5). Empty uses the default four. NOTE: labels are frozen once sent — never put changing values such as HP here (keep those in the body)

inputs.command_prefix.name: Command prefix
inputs.command_prefix.description: The text actually sent on click = prefix + button label (e.g. "/battle ")

inputs.bar_width.name: Bar width
inputs.bar_width.description: How many blocks the HP bar uses (1–40)

outputs.markdown.name: Panel content
outputs.markdown.description: Composed markdown; wire it into "Send message" (Markdown / Button mode)

outputs.keyboard.name: Button
outputs.keyboard.description: Composed button structure; wire it into the "Keyboard" port of "Send message"

group_op.label: Group admin
group_op.description: Unified group admin node (mode switch): mute / mute all / kick / set card / set title / approve friend request / approve join request / leave group / announcement / upload file / pin as essence
group_op.summary: Pick a group management action: mute / kick / mute all / set card / set title / leave / approve friend / approve join / announcement / upload file / pin as essence

inputs.mode.name: Mode
inputs.mode.description: Options: mute / mute all / kick / set card / set title / approve friend request / approve join request / leave group / announcement / upload file / pin as essence

inputs.user_ids.name: QQ numbers (batch)
inputs.user_ids.description: Several QQ numbers for the batch modes, comma or space separated (e.g. 111,222). Used only by "kick batch / blacklist add / blacklist remove"

inputs.enable.name: Enable
inputs.enable.description: Whether to enable mute-all ("mute all" mode)

inputs.flag.name: Flag
inputs.flag.description: Request flag ("approve friend / approve join" modes)

inputs.sub_type.name: Sub type
inputs.sub_type.description: Options: group invite / someone's application ("approve join request" only)

inputs.file_name.name: File name
inputs.file_name.description: File name after upload ("upload file" mode)

inputs.message_id.name: Message ID
inputs.message_id.description: ID of the message to pin as essence ("pin as essence" mode; empty = the current event message)

join_approval.label: Join auto-approval
join_approval.description: Join auto-approval strategies: list / create / update / delete / execute / maintain whitelist
join_approval.summary: Configure auto-approval rules on the official side: which groups, enabled or not, whitelist numbers, plus a manual full scan. Useful when approval must work while offline.

inputs.mode.name: Mode
inputs.mode.description: Options: list strategies / create strategy / update strategy / update whitelist / execute strategy / delete strategy

inputs.strategy_id.name: Strategy ID
inputs.strategy_id.description: Strategy to operate on (get it from "list strategies" first; required for everything except create)

inputs.group_openids.name: Related group openids
inputs.group_openids.description: Group openids to associate (one per line, comma/space separated, up to 100). Only one of this and "Related group numbers" may be filled (the official API rejects both)

inputs.group_ids.name: Related group numbers
inputs.group_ids.description: QQ group numbers to associate (one per line, up to 100). Only one of this and "Related group openids" may be filled; once chosen, later updates must use the same form

inputs.is_enable.name: Enabled
inputs.is_enable.description: Enable / disable (the official API uses the on/off string). Defaults to enabled

inputs.expire_at.name: Expires at
inputs.expire_at.description: RFC3339 timestamp; empty means one year from now

inputs.group_op.name: Group action
inputs.group_op.description: "Update strategy" mode: add or remove related groups (fill the group identifiers above as well)

inputs.op.name: Whitelist action
inputs.op.description: "Update whitelist" mode: add or remove numbers

inputs.whitelist_users.name: Whitelist numbers
inputs.whitelist_users.description: QQ numbers (one per line or comma separated), up to 10000 per call and 100000 in total

inputs.cursor.name: Cursor
inputs.cursor.description: "List strategies" paging cursor (pass the "next cursor" from the previous call)

inputs.limit.name: Page size
inputs.limit.description: "List strategies" only (the official API defaults to 20 and allows at most 50)

outputs.data.name: Data
outputs.data.description: For list: the strategies (strategy_id / related groups / whitelist count / enabled state / expiry); for create: the new strategy id; for execute: an "accepted" note (the official API scans asynchronously, about 10 minutes)

channel_op.label: Channel operations
channel_op.description: QQ channel sub-channels, announcements, pins and reactions
channel_op.summary: Manages a QQ channel: sub-channels, announcements, pinned messages and emoji reactions. The bot must be in the channel with the required permissions; creating/editing/deleting sub-channels needs admin rights.

inputs.mode.name: Mode
inputs.mode.description: Which channel operation to run

inputs.guild_id.name: Guild ID
inputs.guild_id.description: Target guild ID; wire it from the "Message received" trigger output

inputs.channel_id.name: Channel ID
inputs.channel_id.description: Target sub-channel ID; wire it from the "Message received" trigger output

inputs.message_id.name: Message ID
inputs.message_id.description: Target message ID (required for pins and reactions; pass all when deleting a recommend-type announcement)

inputs.type.name: Channel type
inputs.type.description: Only used on creation (category type requires position >= 2)

inputs.parent_id.name: Category ID
inputs.parent_id.description: Leave empty or 0 to keep it outside any category

inputs.speak_permission.name: Speak permission
inputs.speak_permission.description: 0 = none, 1 = everyone, 2 = owner/admins plus listed members

inputs.recommend_channels.name: Recommended channels
inputs.recommend_channels.description: JSON list of recommended sub-channels. Filling it makes this a recommend-type announcement and replaces the whole list; at most 3 per guild, and only channels visible to all members can be recommended. Mutually exclusive with Message ID

inputs.emoji_type.name: Emoji type
inputs.emoji_type.description: System emoji uses an emoji id; emoji uses a code point

inputs.emoji_id.name: Emoji ID
inputs.emoji_id.description: System emoji id (e.g. 4 delighted, 76 like) or an emoji code point

outputs.data.name: Data
outputs.data.description: Query results; includes the new sub-channel id on creation

outputs.error.name: Error
outputs.error.description: Error message (empty = success). Sub-channel changes need admin rights; insufficient permission is reported here

answer_interaction.label: Button acknowledgement
answer_interaction.description: Acknowledge a user button or menu click
answer_interaction.summary: Acknowledges a user button or menu click so the client stops waiting. Without it the client spins until it times out (a fallback acknowledgement is built in). Wire the interaction ID from the "Button click" trigger

inputs.interaction_id.name: Interaction ID
inputs.interaction_id.description: Wire the "Interaction ID" port of the "Button click" trigger

inputs.code.name: Result
inputs.code.description: Result sent back to the client; drives the hint text

menu_config.label: Custom menu
menu_config.description: Query or set the bot's global custom menu
menu_config.summary: Queries or sets the global custom menu (private chat only, shared by all users). Setting replaces the whole menu rather than patching it. At most 10 items; links must start with https.

inputs.mode.name: Mode
inputs.mode.description: Read the current menu, or replace it with a new one

inputs.menu.name: Menu content
inputs.menu.description: Menu structure (required when setting). Item types: switch, send_message, link, or menu for a collapsible submenu (at most 5 sub-items, no further nesting)

outputs.data.name: Data
outputs.data.description: The current menu when reading; includes the menu version when setting

outputs.error.name: Error
outputs.error.description: Error message (empty = success), including count limits and content-safety rejections

panel_config.label: Command panel
panel_config.summary: Manages command panels (private chat / group / text channel / channel DM). List and inspect, or create, edit content, change targets and delete. A panel item fills the input box or opens a link when tapped.

inputs.mode.name: Mode
inputs.mode.description: Which panel operation to run

inputs.scope.name: Scope
inputs.scope.description: Where the panel applies. Text channel and channel DM only support global panels

inputs.panel_id.name: Panel ID
inputs.panel_id.description: Target panel ID (returned by the API on creation)

inputs.target_type.name: Target range
inputs.target_type.description: All targets, or only the listed users/groups (specific targets are private chat and group only)

inputs.user_openids.name: Users
inputs.user_openids.description: OpenIDs of target users for private chat; separate with commas or spaces (at most 20)

inputs.group_openids.name: Groups
inputs.group_openids.description: OpenIDs of target groups; separate with commas or spaces (at most 20)

inputs.panel.name: Panel content
inputs.panel.description: Panel configuration (required for create/update). At most 20 items; item type is command or link, and links must start with https

outputs.data.name: Data
outputs.data.description: Panel data for list/detail; includes panel_id on creation

outputs.error.name: Error
outputs.error.description: Error message (empty = success), including invalid scope/range and count limits

api_call.label: API call
api_call.summary: Call a low-level protocol API (e.g. get_group_list) — for advanced protocol work

inputs.action.name: API name
inputs.action.description: Name of the protocol API to call

outputs.result.name: Result
outputs.result.description: API result

http_request.label: HTTP request
http_request.summary: Make an HTTP request to fetch external data — for weather lookups, calling APIs, or third-party services

inputs.headers.name: Headers
inputs.headers.description: Headers JSON object, e.g. {"Authorization":"Bearer xxx"}; fill {} or leave empty for no custom headers

inputs.response_format.name: Response format
inputs.response_format.description: Response format (options: auto / JSON / text / binary)

outputs.text.name: Text
outputs.text.description: Raw response body text (ALWAYS a string — JSON responses keep their original text too, so you can re-parse it or paste it straight into a message). Empty string when the request fails

file_operate.label: File op

inputs.expression.name: Expression
inputs.expression.description:
Expression (Python-style syntax, translated to JS for evaluation at runtime — the same evaluator as "Conditional Branch"). Note: variable names cannot be reserved words (such as def/class/import/new/in/true).
[Available functions] Must be written as functions, not methods: len/int/float/str/bool/abs/min/max/sum/round/clamp/range/list/dict/json/now/time/random/randint/choice/upper/lower/strip/replace/split/join/startswith/endswith/contains/format/sort/reverse/keys/values/items/get/to_json/from_json
Common examples:
  · Damage: clamp(atk * 2 - def * 0.5, 1, 999)
  · Random: randint(1, 6) / choice(["rock","paper","scissors"])
  · Strings: upper(name) / len(s) / "prefix" in s / f"{v}k"
  · Dict field: get(monster, "hp", 0)
  · Ternary: 10 if hp > 0 else 0
[Not supported] Python method calls must become function calls (write upper(s), not s.upper(); or use native JS s.toUpperCase()); list comprehensions [x for x in lst] (use JS lst.filter(...) / lst.map(...)); f-string format specs (write round(v, 2), not f"{v:,.2f}"). The underlying engine is JS, so Math.*, arrow functions and array methods all work; process/require/window/eval are blocked. A failed evaluation writes the error to the "Error" port instead of silently returning a falsy value.

A JSON dict or dict object, e.g. {"atk":100,"defense":50,"hp":200}. Can be wired directly from "Time op", "Persistent op" and similar outputs.
[Two uses] (1) Single expression: the dict keys become variable names you can write directly (e.g. atk + defense).
(2) **Shared context for batch formulas** (important): in “batch formulas” mode each formula cannot see the others’ local variables, so any common setup must be computed once and wired here — otherwise every formula has to repeat it (measured on a real project: without this, 54% of all formula code was duplicated preamble; the worst node repeated the same 1,700 characters 4 times).
How: wire an expression that returns a dict (e.g. `({st: ..., row: ...})`), then write st / row directly in each formula.

inputs.mode.description: What to look up: member profiles / group info / group lists / bot status (grouped under "Group info" and "Member")

inputs.group_id.name: Group
inputs.group_id.description: Target group ID (leave empty for the current group)

inputs.user_id.name: QQ number
inputs.user_id.description: QQ number to look up (leave empty for the sender)

inputs.cursor.name: Cursor
inputs.cursor.description: The "next page cursor" returned by the previous call for "member list / join requests / blacklist"; leave empty for the first page

outputs.result.name: Result
outputs.result.description: The result (object or list, depending on the selected mode)

outputs.card.name: Group card
outputs.card.description: "User name" mode: group card (group chats only)

outputs.next_cursor.name: Next cursor
outputs.next_cursor.description: Next page cursor for "member list / join requests / blacklist" (empty = no more pages)

outputs.is_admin.name: Is admin
outputs.is_admin.description: Whether the user is an admin or the group owner

outputs.recv_msg_setting.name: Receive mode
outputs.recv_msg_setting.description: In "bot group status" mode: the message-receiving setting (for example only_mention)

outputs.mute_mode.name: Mute mode
outputs.mute_mode.description: "Group mute state" mode: none (off) / always (always muted) / schedule (scheduled)

outputs.mute_rules.name: Mute rules
outputs.mute_rules.description: In "group mute status" mode: the raw official mute rules, passed through unchanged

outputs.muted_members.name: Muted members
outputs.muted_members.description: In "group mute status" mode: the list of individually muted members

outputs.success.name: Success
outputs.success.description: Whether the call succeeded (API-backed modes may fail)

format_text.label: Text template
format_text.description: Build text with named placeholders; supports variables_json plus var1~var8
format_text.summary: Build a text template from named variables via variables_json; var1~var8 remain supported for backward compatibility

inputs.variables_json.name: Named variables
inputs.variables_json.description: A JSON dict or dict object. Can be wired directly from "Time op", "Expression eval" and similar outputs

outputs.result.name: Result
outputs.result.description: The substituted text

regex_extract.label: Regex extract
regex_extract.description: Extract the parts of a text that match a regular expression
regex_extract.summary: Extract matches from text with a regular expression; supports capture groups and an all-matches list

inputs.group.name: Capture group
inputs.group.description: 0 returns the whole match; 1 and above select the Nth capture group

inputs.as_list.name: Return list
inputs.as_list.description: True returns a list of all matches; False returns only the first

outputs.result.name: Result
outputs.result.description: Match result (string or list)
